title: What Staircase Cities Is
definition: Staircase Cities: cities climbing steep hillsides in terraced steps.
description:
Staircase Cities — Signature Edition: cities climbing steep hillsides in terraced steps. This is the JAH-original vision, designed from first principles and labeled as Signature speculation throughout.

The Signature stair hulls program starts where public roadmaps stop. Where public research asks what is fundable, the Signature line asks what is buildable: terraced districts rethought, funicular transit rebuilt, slope engineering reimagined for the century ahead. This edition mirrors the public database record for record — concept, components, milestones, demos, drills, alliance, roadmap — but every entry is the Signature take: bolder timelines, integrated systems thinking, and the step blocks ambition that defines the Signature line.

title: The Signature Vision: Staircase Cities
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Staircase Cities.
description:
The Signature vision of Staircase Cities does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature stair hulls program, charter one: master terraced districts at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale funicular transit manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate slope engineering systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Staircase Cities becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

title: The stair hulls Grid
definition: The stair hulls Grid: a load-bearing component of Staircase Cities.
description:
The urban backbone: power, water, data and logistics woven into one terraced districts grid that the stair hulls district runs on.

In the Staircase Cities architecture, the stair hulls grid is load-bearing: without it the stair hulls fails outright — Staircase Cities stops being Staircase Cities at all. Builders sequence this piece early because every other component assumes it works. In the Signature architecture this piece is designed first-class, not bolted on.

Maturity varies: some deployments of this piece exist today in simpler forms, while the full Staircase Cities-grade version remains a research target. The readiness estimator in this database scores it honestly.

t: 2030 — The first stair hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first stair hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Staircase Cities roadmap.
description:
The first stair hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its terraced districts grid and funicular transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the terraced districts results have to replicate outside the lab, funicular transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and slope engineering operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed terraced districts demonstrations, funicular transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting slope engineering uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Staircase Cities
definition: Estimates Staircase Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Staircase Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a stair hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Staircase Cities Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Staircase Cities operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Staircase Cities installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 30786 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where terraced districts monitoring, funicular transit redundancy, or slope engineering maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Staircase Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Staircase Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Staircase Cities — cities climbing steep hillsides in terraced steps.

Phase 1 — Prove (terraced districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (funicular transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (slope engineering): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (step blocks): stair hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and hillsides-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
